hook.line: News reports and official letters love to say "so far" in a serious way. *Hasta la fecha* tells you the situation stands as of today, and it leaves the door open for change.
hook.es: Hasta el momento Altamira no ha dicho nada.
hook.en: So far Altamira hasn't said anything.

examples.es: Hasta la fecha no se ha encontrado al responsable.
examples.en: To date, the person responsible has not been found.

examples.es: Hasta el momento no hay heridos.
examples.en: So far there are no casualties.
For now, we're carrying on as before.

rule:
*Hasta la fecha* and *hasta el momento* mean "up to now". They sound formal, like news or official letters.

They go with the *he / ha* past: *no se ha encontrado*, *no ha dicho nada*. The point is that it still stands today.

*De momento* means "for now" and is more casual. It goes with the present: *De momento seguimos igual.*

Note the little words: *la fecha*, *el momento*, never swapped.
smallPrint: Teachers call these temporal adverbials: phrases that tell you up to which point in time something is true.

readAndPick.es: Hasta el momento Altamira no ha dicho nada.
options: Altamira said nothing at that moment.
So far Altamira hasn't said anything.
Altamira will say nothing.

readAndPick.es: Hasta la fecha nadie ha firmado el contrato.
options: To date nobody has signed the contract.
Nobody signed the contract on that date.
Nobody will sign the contract.
We stayed the same last time.
We will stay the same forever.
For now, we're carrying on as before.

readAndPick.es: Hasta el momento no hay heridos.
options: Nobody was injured at that moment.
So far there are no casualties.
There will be no casualties.

readAndPick.es: Hasta la fecha no he recibido respuesta.
options: To date I haven't received a reply.
I never received a reply.
I will not receive a reply.

options: The person responsible was found on that date.
To date, the person responsible has not been found.
The person responsible will be found.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hasta ___ fecha nadie ha firmado el contrato.* (*la* or *el*) To date nobody has signed the contract.
yourTurn.answer: Hasta la fecha nadie ha firmado el contrato.
accept: Hasta la fecha, nadie ha firmado el contrato.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hasta el momento Altamira no ___ dicho nada.* (*ha* or *dijo*) So far Altamira hasn't said anything.
yourTurn.answer: Hasta el momento Altamira no ha dicho nada.
accept: Hasta el momento, Altamira no ha dicho nada.
yourTurn.why: "So far" looks back from today, so the *ha dicho* past fits.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: So far there are no casualties.
yourTurn.answer: Hasta el momento no hay heridos.
accept: Hasta el momento, no hay heridos.
yourTurn.why: With "so far" the present *hay* simply states how things stand now.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: To date I haven't received a reply.
yourTurn.answer: Hasta la fecha no he recibido respuesta.
accept: Hasta la fecha, no he recibido respuesta.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: For now, we're carrying on as before.
Change it to the casual one: *Hasta el momento no hay noticias.* (say "for now")
yourTurn.why: Casual "for now" is *de momento*, and the rest stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about nobody: *Hasta la fecha el dueño ha firmado el contrato.*
yourTurn.answer: Hasta la fecha nadie ha firmado el contrato.
accept: Hasta la fecha, nadie ha firmado el contrato.
yourTurn.why: *Nadie* replaces the subject, and no extra *no* is needed before the verb.

pitfalls.wrong: Hasta la momento no hay heridos.
pitfalls.right: Hasta el momento no hay heridos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Momento* is masculine, so it is *el momento*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hasta fecha no se ha encontrado al responsable.
pitfalls.right: Hasta la fecha no se ha encontrado al responsable.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English drops the article ("to date"), but Spanish keeps *la*.
Almost. For "for now", Spanish says *de momento*.

personal: Think of something that has not happened yet in your life or your week. Say it: *Hasta la fecha no he…*.
